title: Vitamins and supplements: what the NHS says
question_forms: Which vitamins and supplements should I take?
tradition_says: Tonics, multivitamins and iron "blood builders" are widely used for tiredness, hair and skin, and many families keep a cupboard of supplements.

layer1.plain_answer: The NHS says most people get all the nutrients they need from a varied, balanced diet. The main exception for you is vitamin D: people with African, African-Caribbean or South Asian backgrounds should consider a daily supplement all year. Do not take iron without a blood test, and tell a pharmacist about any herbal remedy if you take other medicines.

do.text: Aim to get your nutrients from a varied and balanced diet first.
Consider a daily vitamin D supplement all year if your background is African, African-Caribbean or South Asian; everyone should consider one in autumn and winter.
Ask for a full blood count if you are tired, short of breath or have heavy periods, before any iron tablets.
Check with a pharmacist before taking a herbal medicine if you already take other medicines.

avoid.text: Taking iron tablets without a blood test: the UK's NHS has a doctor recommend treatment once the cause is found.
Herbal medicines if you are pregnant or breastfeeding, have kidney or liver problems, or take medicines such as statins, diabetes or blood pressure tablets, unless a pharmacist has checked.

see_someone_when: Tiredness, breathlessness, headaches or paler skin that is not settling (doctor, for a blood test).
You take prescribed medicine and want to add a herbal remedy (pharmacist).

tested.design: Cohort study of total vitamin D, vitamin D-binding protein and bone density
tested.finding: Mean total 25(OH)D was 15.6 against 25.8 ng/mL in Black against white participants, and vitamin D-binding protein was 168 against 337 micrograms/mL; Black participants had higher bone mineral density. Genetic variants explained about 79% of variation in the binding protein.

source.authors: Powe CE, Evans MK, Wenger J, Zonderman AB et al

tested.note: Reused from the vitamin D entry; this card gives NHS advice, not a verdict on the contested bone-health evidence.

tier_driver: Which supplements to take: NHS guidance, with no trial opened for the general advice; the contested vitamin D evidence is in its own entry.
tier_note: D because the headline is general guidance with no tested claim in Black adults for supplements as a whole; the vitamin D evidence is separate. The NHS vitamins page I opened was last reviewed in August 2020 with review overdue, so treat it as dated.
harm_note: No harm signal for the advice on this card. The UK's NHS warns that iron and some herbal remedies need a test or a pharmacist check.
evidence_summary: The NHS vitamins and minerals page says most people get what they need from a balanced diet. The NHS vitamin D page says people with African, African-Caribbean or South Asian backgrounds may not make enough vitamin D from sunlight and should consider a daily supplement through the year. Iron deficiency anaemia is confirmed by a blood test before treatment. Whether a vitamin D supplement helps Black adults is contested; see the vitamin D entry.
measured_variables: Self-identified race in the vitamin D cohort, a stand-in for vitamin D-binding protein genotype
gaps: Not opened: folic acid and pregnancy supplement pages; B12 and calcium for vegetarians or dairy avoiders; any trial of multivitamins in Black adults; the UK's NHS vitamins overview page I opened has a review date of 3 August 2023, now past. The card gives no doses; the vitamin D page names one but I left it out. Hair and skin supplements are in their own entries.

sources.authors: Powe CE, Evans MK, Wenger J, Zonderman AB et al
